title: pareto-frontier-maxlen-batch-cache-scan-feb2026
body:
Purpose:
This note captures an exploratory scan of the latency / cost / quality Pareto frontier for a candidate model during onboarding. We varied three operating axes (batch size, prefix-cache window, and max_new_tokens) to surface practical operating points and detect any regressions relative to the onboarding baseline. The goal: recommend candidate configs for production smoke tests and identify configurations that violate SLO or quality constraints.

Background and motivation:
- Recent onboarding (AM-1724) ran a limited sweep but left gaps at long max_new_tokens and combined high-batch+prefetch regimes. Teams requested a focused Pareto scan to expose knee points for latency vs. cost vs. QA accuracy on our standard promptset.
- We treat QA accuracy on the labeled promptset (500-shot mixed-domain prompts used in onboarding) as the primary quality gate. We also track answer-precision and hallucination-rate proxies.

Experiment design (brief):
- Model: baseline model-A (7B fp16) and quantized variant model-A-q4 (7B q4_0).
- Axes scanned in grid: batch_size in {1,2,4,8,16}; prefix_cache_size in {0,32,64,128} tokens; max_new_tokens in {64,128,256,512}.
- Hardware: Dedicated v2-GPU (32GB) instance used for consistent kernel selection. Same runtime image used across runs.
- Traffic shape: synthetic request stream sampled from onboard promptset distribution; 20k requests per configuration to capture p99 tails.
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), median tokens/sec (throughput), cost_per_1M_output_tokens (USD), QA_accuracy (%) on evaluation promptset, hallucination_rate (%) estimated by automated reference-checking.
- Regression detection rule: a quality drop >1.5 percentage points relative to the onboarding baseline flags the config as a potential regression.

Key findings (summary):
1) Pareto shape: a clear two-segment frontier emerges: (A) low-latency region (batch_size<=2, prefix_cache>=64, max_new_tokens<=128) gives best p90 latency while keeping cost moderate; (B) high-throughput region (batch_size>=8, prefix_cache<=32) reduces cost/token by ~30% but increases p90 latency by 2.5x.
2) Cache wins are context-dependent: enabling prefix_cache=64 produced a 18–28% drop in p90 latency for repeated-context prompts (high prefix overlap), and a 12–15% cost reduction from lower compute per request (fewer re-computed attention windows). For low-overlap prompts, cache gives negligible benefit and can increase variability.
3) Max_new_tokens scaling: moving from 128->512 increases p50 by ~40% and p90 by ~60% on average; cost per 1M output tokens increases almost linearly with max_new_tokens. Quality impact for long outputs: QA_accuracy drops 0.6–1.2 points at 512 tokens when combined with quantized variant.
4) Quantized model tradeoffs: model-A-q4 reduces cost/token by ~22–27% vs fp16 for equivalent config points; QA_accuracy shows a small but measurable drop (mean 1.8 percentage points) when max_new_tokens>=256 and batch_size>=8. This exceeded our regression threshold in multiple configs.

Representative datapoints (selected operating points):
- Config L1 (low-latency): model-A fp16, batch=1, cache=64, max_new=128 -> p50=82ms, p90=130ms, p99=310ms, throughput=140 tok/s, cost/1M=12.8 USD, QA_acc=88.7%, hallucination_rate=4.1%
- Config T1 (throughput/cheap): model-A-q4, batch=16, cache=0, max_new=128 -> p50=210ms, p90=520ms, p99=1230ms, throughput=620 tok/s, cost/1M=9.4 USD, QA_acc=86.1%, hallucination_rate=6.0%
- Config R1 (long outputs): model-A fp16, batch=2, cache=128, max_new=512 -> p50=180ms, p90=290ms, p99=710ms, throughput=95 tok/s, cost/1M=36.2 USD, QA_acc=87.5%, hallucination_rate=5.0%
- Config Qfail (regression-flagged): model-A-q4, batch=8, cache=32, max_new=256 -> p50=130ms, p90=360ms, p99=980ms, throughput=420 tok/s, cost/1M=22.6 USD, QA_acc=86.0% (baseline was 87.9%) -> delta=-1.9 pts -> flagged

Interpretation and practical guidance:
- Default production guardrail: prefer small-batch low-latency configs for interactive features (batch<=2, prefix_cache>=64 when prefix overlap>30%, max_new_tokens<=128). These hit p90<=150ms on our hardware and keep QA drop <0.5 points.
- Cost-optimized path: for high-throughput asynchronous workloads, choose quantized variant with batch>=8 and cache disabled or small; accept higher p90 but lower $/token. However, enforce a QA recheck on representative long-output prompts: if QA drops by >1.5 points, blacklist that combination for customer-facing use.
- Max_new_tokens caution: long outputs are expensive — unless product requires >256 tokens, prefer chunking strategies or streaming to keep latency/cost reasonable. When required, prefer fp16 over quantized for long outputs to avoid larger quality regressions.

Regression notes and actions:
- The quantized variant exceeded the regression threshold in 4 out of 60 tested configs (all with max_new_tokens>=256 and batch>=4). Root cause hypothesis: quantization-induced degradation compounds on longer autoregressive decoding and with larger internal KV cache pressure; further profiling needed on attention kernel fidelity at high sequence lengths.
- Action items:
  - A1: Run targeted per-layer logit-diff tracing for flagged config Qfail to determine where distributional shift occurs (owner: Claire, due 2026-02-26).
  - A2: Add a focused promptset of long-output QA items (200 prompts, varied domains) to the onboarding eval to stress test quantized variants (owner: Jamal, due 2026-03-03).
  - A3: Implement automated pre-deploy gate that refuses quantized model for any rollout config where max_new_tokens>=256 unless an explicit QA override is provided and passing metrics exist (owner: Maya, due 2026-03-10).

Anomalies and caveats observed:
- One run (batch=4, cache=128, max_new=256, fp16) exhibited elevated p99 due to OS-level GC event on the test host; we excluded that single-day run from aggregated p99 numbers.
- Cache benefits are workload-dependent: for chat-like reuse patterns the 64-token cache is often near-optimal; for generative creative prompts with near-zero prefix overlap, cache adds memory overhead without latency wins. Recommend heuristic cache_policy: enable prefix_cache only when observed prefix overlap > 25% over a 10-minute sliding window.

Recommended immediate defaults for onboarding and smoke tests:
- Smoke default (fast feedback): model-A fp16, batch=1, cache=64, max_new=128 (as L1).
- Cost-smoke (throughput): model-A-q4, batch=8, cache=0, max_new=128 but only for internal/non-customer workloads until targeted QA tests pass.

Next steps:
- Extend sweep to include kernel variants (attention-fused kernels vs. generic) and another hardware type (v2-GPU-XL) to generalize frontier shifts.
- Add streaming throughput experiments to measure perceived latency under long outputs (first-token latency vs full-sequence).
- Close loop with runtime team to expose automated cache-enable heuristics based on measured prefix-overlap signals.

Appendix: links to raw CSVs and dashboards:
- Raw metric dump: GITHUB:pr/engineering/serving-runtime#789 -> artifacts/csvs/pareto_scan_feb2026.zip
- Dashboard: CONFLUENCE:ML-ONBOARD-188 -> visualizations / pareto-frontier page

Notes-to-self (informal):
- We should try a micro-probe of cache eviction TTLs (e.g., 1s vs 10s) — might help high-burst interactive workloads.
- Consider adding an eval metric that penalizes long-answer hallucinations more heavily when max_new_tokens>256.
